newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-New Aussie downtrend looms as 75cts cracks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-New Aussie downtrend looms as 75cts cracks.

text.p: *Whole new downtrend threatening after 75 support finally cracked under weight of Swiss, German and NY bank selling
*Offers now holding a thin line at $0.7480 and approaching oversold on short term charts, so some chance of a bounce
*But chart indicators all bearish and only matter of time before $0.7450 seen, enroute to $0.7380 and even 73 cents
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar was under water at US$0.7486/91 after sinking from US$0.7513/18 late here Monday.
The dip took it below 75 cents for the first time since February 1996 and brought losses since the surprise Reserve Bank rate cut on May 23 to 2-3/4 cents or 3.6 percent.

The start of the entire downtrend can be traced back to a peak of US$0.8005 in mid-March, so total losses amount to more than five cents or 6.4 percent. In trade weighted terms the decline has been even larger at around 7.2 percent.
But the overnight break meant it was far from over with some analysts tipping another two to three month decline to 73 cents.

The latter is the 1996 trough reached in late January of that year. There were support levels above there including US$0.7450, US$0.7420, US$0.7380 and US$0.7350 but analysts felt the low would act as a major attractor now.
The currency would need to clear the resistance band at US$0.7630-7680 to reverse the downtrend, they added.

This looked a tough task while speculation of another easing gave it such a hefty interest differential to bear. Forward A$ rates were up at positive levels no trader could remember and three month futures showed the market expected official rates here to be cut to 5.0 percent and U.S. rates hiked to 5.75 pct.
Most analysts expect the RBA will stand pat for the moment and see how domestic data next month pans out and how policy develops in the U.S.
But the market is taking no chances after being badly burned by the last easing and will be on alert at every 9.30 am RBA operation from now on, including this morning.

There is little in the way of domestic data this week, or next for that matter, and today holds just the quarterly data on dwelling commencements which are seen up around 5.0 percent. Also out is ABARE's quarterly forecast of Australia's commodity production for 1996/97 and 97/89. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
